title: How to plan creator merchandise your audience will actually wear
seoTitle: Planning a First Creator Merchandise Drop
description: Turn a community idea into a wearable first product. Choose a garment, test the design, gather size information and prepare the pack for launch.
author: BEWE4R team
intro: Start with a reason your audience would wear the item after launch week. A phrase your viewers recognise can make a good design, but it still needs a garment that fits their everyday life. Choose one product you can show, fit and explain convincingly before adding variations.

bodyHtml:
Turn audience feedback into a product decision

Suppose a creator runs a drawing channel. Viewers repeatedly ask about a sketch on the studio wall. A tee featuring that line drawing may make a stronger first item than several garments carrying the channel name. Show two interpretations at the intended print scale and ask which one people would actually wear. Keep the garment choice, artwork choice and size question separate. A vote for an illustration gives you no reliable size breakdown.

Build the sample your launch needs

Photograph the approved piece on a person and show a close-up of the artwork. Record the sample size and the finished garment measurements you use for the product page. If the tee in the photo is a prototype, note any detail that will change before bulk. A later supplier substitution should trigger a check of the photos and description as well as the technical file.

Launch taskEvidence to have before publishing
Product descriptionFinal style, fit notes, colour and artwork
Size selectionMeasurements for the offered sizes and an explanation of how they were taken
Stock or pre-order choiceConfirmed variants, production conditions and an owner for customer updates
PackingA folded sample with the correct external size identifier

Decide what your team can fulfil

If you intend to ship the drop yourself, practise picking an order from two similar piles. Can you tell a medium from a large without opening each bag? Do the names in your shop match the wording on the cartons? A simple test with two colours and a mixed-size order will reveal whether the product codes work for somebody who did not help invent them.

What if your audience picked a design that looks poor at garment size?

Show a finished-scale trial to a few people who recognise the original artwork. Ask what they can read and identify without an explanation. Thin text may disappear while the main symbol still works. Keep a record of which elements the artist approves for simplification before product photographs or pre-orders go live.

Prepare the next update before launch

Choose the person who can tell customers when a sample is approved, when a variant is held and when goods have actually been received. Give them the latest production information and a place to record changes. If the drop uses pre-orders, use our pre-order planning guide to work through the size split. Discuss a creator merchandise project with BEWE4R.
